invariant.owner_quote: Neither side may claim authority merely because it can read the other's tables.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: Apply projection events idempotently: commit the derived row and its cursor atomically, and disable outbound side effects during rebuild.

alternative.owner_quote: Revisit the separation when command contention, projection lag or rebuild duration outweighs the read benefit, and prefer one model when that case cannot be made.

mechanism.owner_quote: In event sourcing, a durable append-only record of domain facts becomes an authoritative input to reconstruct the present state.
mechanism.reason: Defines the append-only event history and replay reconstruction.

invariant.owner_quote: Rebuilds must check offset continuity and event schema compatibility.
invariant.reason: States a must-hold rebuild precondition for snapshots and replay.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: Replaying a historical event sequence under different event semantics may not produce the same result; versioned event handlers and invariant rules must be specified.
failure_recovery.reason: Identifies replay divergence and prescribes versioned handlers and invariant rules to contain it.

alternative.owner_quote: State-stored CRUD with an audit log, CDC/outbox or event notification may be preferable when full replay is unnecessary, event-schema ownership is absent or external side effects cannot be isolated.

mechanism.owner_quote: A domain event publishes a committed business fact to other owners.

invariant.owner_quote: Use it when the fact has identity, version and causation

failure_recovery.owner_quote: Duplicate, late, out-of-order and schema-evolved events are normal.

alternative.owner_quote: A synchronous call or command message is preferable when event fan-out and eventual consistency exceed the decoupling benefit.

mechanism.owner_quote: A saga is a long-running business protocol across independent owners.
mechanism.reason: Defines a long-running protocol across independent owners.

invariant.owner_quote: The invariant is one authority and one effect identity per step; the saga never claims atomicity or rollback.
invariant.reason: Requires one authority and one effect identity per step without atomicity or rollback.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: A lost acknowledgment is an unknown outcome, not a failure, and a failed compensation remains a repair item.
failure_recovery.reason: Treats a lost acknowledgment as unknown and failed compensation as a repair item.

alternative.owner_quote: Use one local transaction when all effects fit one owner, or two-phase commit when participants can hold prepared state and atomic visibility is mandatory.

mechanism.owner_quote: Participants react to one another's events; the protocol is distributed across those reactions, not held in a central state machine.

invariant.owner_quote: It needs correlation identity, deduplication, dead-letter handling, versioned event contracts and a per-step timeout policy

failure_recovery.owner_quote: Long chains, hidden coupling and conflicting compensations are the failure modes; a trace shows correlation, not durable business truth.

alternative.owner_quote: Orchestration or a single local transaction may be preferable when steps need central visibility, when compensation ordering must be centrally enforced, or when compensations cannot be made safe.

mechanism.owner_quote: An orchestrator persists a state machine and sends commands to participants.
mechanism.reason: States the mechanism, invariant, failure or alternative.

invariant.owner_quote: Its guarantees are only as strong as versioned state persistence, activity semantics, timer reliability and recovery configuration.
invariant.reason: Bounds guarantees by versioned state, activity semantics, timers and recovery configuration.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: Operational failure appears as a lost coordinator, a history that cannot advance, or an activity applied twice.
failure_recovery.reason: States the mechanism, invariant, failure or alternative.

alternative.owner_quote: Prefer one transaction when every effect shares an owner and a database.
alternative.reason: Names a single transaction when every effect shares one owner and database.

mechanism.owner_quote: A compensating transaction is a new business action that creates an acceptable counter-effect; it is not rollback and it can fail.
mechanism.reason: Defines compensation as a new action, not rollback.

invariant.owner_quote: The domain must determine which actions are reversible and which require manual reconciliation.
invariant.reason: Leaves reversibility and manual reconciliation to the domain.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: A release itself can fail; a delivered message cannot be un-delivered; the kit may already have been handed to a participant.
failure_recovery.reason: Names irreversible delivery and already-released artifacts as repair items.

alternative.owner_quote: Orchestration or a single local transaction may be preferable when steps need central visibility, when compensation ordering must be centrally enforced, or when compensations cannot be made safe.
alternative.reason: Names the alternative and reversal condition.

mechanism.owner_quote: An outbox is a durable publication queue inside the state store.
mechanism.reason: States the mechanism, invariant, failure or alternative.

invariant.owner_quote: The business row and an intent row commit together
invariant.reason: States the mechanism, invariant, failure or alternative.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: A crash after publish before completion duplicates
failure_recovery.reason: States the mechanism, invariant, failure or alternative.

alternative.owner_quote: Use an outbox when the lost-publication and duplicate-effect risk justifies relay complexity.
alternative.reason: States the mechanism, invariant, failure or alternative.

mechanism.owner_quote: An inbox can persist a consumer's processed-event identity and business effect together in **one local transaction**.
mechanism.reason: Persists processed-event identity and business effect in one local transaction.

invariant.owner_quote: The identity must include the correct subscriber and event/effect scope; two different consumers legitimately process the same event into different local states.
invariant.reason: Scopes identity by subscriber and event/effect.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: a notification consumer writes a processed marker then crashes before making an external non-idempotent send. On redelivery it may falsely skip the missing send. Reversing the order may send twice.
failure_recovery.reason: Names marker-before-send crash windows that can skip or duplicate a send.

alternative.owner_quote: A unique constraint or conditional insert on effect identity, a producer outbox, or an idempotent downstream API may be preferable when the inbox table and retention cost exceed the duplicate-impact risk.

invariant.owner_quote: The outcome record and business effect must commit together; a later separate write leaves a window for duplicate execution.
